navigation.summary: Know how `<Link>` prefetches, what the client cache keeps, how the `next/navigation` hooks behave, and how `redirect`, `notFound` and `router.refresh` interact with caches and history in the Next.js 16 App Router.
points: `<Link>` prefetches in production only. By default static routes are prefetched in full, and dynamic routes down to the nearest `loading.js`. `prefetch={true}` prefetches the full route, and App Router `prefetch={false}` disables viewport and hover prefetching.

The client cache stores RSC payloads in memory. `staleTimes.dynamic` defaults to 0 s (since v15) and `staleTimes.static` to 5 min, which also covers `prefetch={true}` and `router.prefetch()`. Back/forward reuses cached pages whatever `staleTimes` says.

`router.refresh()` re-renders Server Components and keeps unaffected client and browser state. It clears the client cache for the route, but not server caches: use `revalidatePath`, `revalidateTag` or `updateTag` for those.

`redirect()` gives 307 (`permanentRedirect` gives 308). In a Server Action it does a client-side navigation with JS, or a 303 for a native form POST, and defaults to `push` history there (`replace` elsewhere). It throws, so code after it never runs.

`useSearchParams` on a statically prerendered page needs a `<Suspense>` boundary, or `next build` fails. Layouts never receive `searchParams`. With Cache Components, `usePathname` and `useParams` suspend for params not covered by `generateStaticParams`.

`useSelectedLayoutSegment` returns the active segment one level below the calling layout (or `null`). `useSelectedLayoutSegments` returns an array that includes route groups, with catch-all matches joined into one string.

With Cache Components, pages are hidden with `<Activity>` (up to 3 routes), so state survives navigation. Use URL-derived state, `bfcacheId` keys, or `window.location.href` for logout when state must reset.
traps: Putting `redirect()` or `notFound()` inside `try/catch` swallows the framework error. Call them outside the `try`, or use `unstable_rethrow(e)`.
Calling `revalidatePath` after `redirect` does nothing, because `redirect` throws. Always invalidate first.
`prefetch={true}` on a live dynamic page makes clicks reuse a payload up to 5 minutes old (`staleTimes.static`).
